title: Prehistoric Specimen Material Lab
description: The user operates a virtual material science laboratory where a ShaderBall serves as a calibration target and a MosquitoInAmber specimen floats nearby as the subject of analysis. The user adjusts shader parameters on the ShaderBall to match and then transfer custom material properties onto the amber specimen, cycling through roughness, metalness, emissive glow, refraction index, and tint color, then confirming each parameter to complete the calibration sequence.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements a Prehistoric Specimen Material Lab. Load ShaderBall.glb on the left side of the scene and MosquitoInAmber.glb on the right, both using GLTFLoader. Place a PerspectiveCamera at (0, 1.5, 5) looking at the origin. Add an HDR-style lighting rig with one DirectionalLight, one warm PointLight near the amber, and a soft AmbientLight. Both models should slowly rotate on their Y-axis. Create an HTML overlay panel on the left with six controls: (1) a roughness slider 0-1, (2) a metalness slider 0-1, (3) an emissive intensity slider 0-2, (4) a refraction index slider 1.0-2.5 mapped to opacity and ior if using MeshPhysicalMaterial, (5) a color picker for tint color, and (6) a Confirm button. The workflow requires the user to: Step 1 - adjust roughness and observe the ShaderBall update in real time. Step 2 - adjust metalness similarly. Step 3 - set emissive intensity causing the ShaderBall to glow. Step 4 - tune the refraction index slider. Step 5 - pick a tint color. Step 6 - press Confirm to transfer all current material parameters from the ShaderBall onto every mesh in the MosquitoInAmber model with a smooth 1.5-second tween using simple lerp in the animation loop. Validate each parameter has been changed from its default before enabling the Confirm button. After transfer completes, display a success banner reading Material Calibration Complete. Replace all materials on both models with MeshPhysicalMaterial on load so sliders work uniformly. Use OrbitControls for camera interaction. Ensure the scene has a dark gradient background using scene.background set to a Color of 0x1a1a2e. Add a subtle grid helper on the ground plane for spatial reference.
